title: “Research”
My research sits at the intersection of electrochemical engineering, transport phenomena, complex-fluid mechanics, and physics-based computation. The projects below are related by a common question: how do local material and transport processes determine device-scale performance?

title: Research
text:
Stress-Limited Hydrodynamics
Classical rotating-disk transport relies on well-defined Newtonian hydrodynamics. Yield-stress fluids introduce an additional difficulty: part of the fluid may remain unyielded, so the active flow domain can itself become part of the solution.
My modeling work investigates:

von Kármán and two-disk rotating-flow frameworks
Bingham and Herschel–Bulkley constitutive behavior
nonlinear boundary-value problems and continuation
finite confinement and breakdown of global similarity
yielded / unyielded regions
comparison between reduced models and COMSOL
implications for mass-transfer boundary layers


Current physical picture: In confined yield-stress flow, the yielded-layer thickness can emerge as a local hydrodynamic length scale rather than the full geometric gap.

title: Research
text:
Particle Suspension Dynamics
I am beginning a separate computational research direction involving Stokesian Dynamics and particle-suspension modeling under the guidance of Dr. Madhu V. Majji.
The immediate purpose is to build depth in particle-scale suspension mechanics rather than force the method into the electrochemical suspension-electrode framework.
Topics of interest include:

low-Reynolds-number particle hydrodynamics
many-body hydrodynamic interactions
Brownian and non-Brownian suspension behavior
particle microstructure under flow
pair and structural statistics
suspension stress and rheological response
links between particle-scale dynamics and continuum descriptions

As this project develops, validated results and public benchmark examples will be added here.

title: Projects

Yield-Stress Rotating-Flow Modeling
Developed reduced-order numerical models and finite-element simulations for rotating Newtonian, Bingham, and Herschel–Bulkley flows.
Key computational elements include:

nonlinear boundary-value solvers
continuation methods
similarity and scaling analysis
finite-geometry COMSOL models
yielded / unyielded region analysis
systematic comparison with prior literature

title: Projects
text:
Coupled Fluid–Particle Heat Transfer
Built an ANSYS Fluent + Discrete Phase Method model for heat and momentum transfer in a serpentine microtube. The model examined single-phase and dilute particle-laden cases, including two-way momentum and energy coupling.

title: Projects
text:
Corrosion Under Insulation Modeling
Developed COMSOL finite-element models for oxygen transport and corrosion in thin electrolyte films relevant to corrosion-under-insulation environments.
Topics: diffusion, electrochemical transport, multiphysics coupling, thin-film modeling.

title: About
text:
I am a PhD researcher in Chemical Engineering at Ohio University working with Dr. Madhu V. Majji.
My technical interests are centered on problems where transport, material microstructure, and device performance are strongly coupled. I enjoy working across the traditional boundary between experiment and computation: building experimental systems, developing physical models, and using each to interrogate the other.

title: About
text:
Background
Before graduate school, I studied Chemical and Electrochemical Engineering at the CSIR–Central Electrochemical Research Institute (CECRI) in India. My earlier research included aqueous zinc-ion batteries, lithium- and sodium-ion cathodes, supercapacitors, and electrochemical materials characterization.
My PhD work has increasingly shifted toward:

electrochemical reactor engineering
suspension rheology and complex fluids
mass and charge transport
mechanistic / continuum modeling
multiphysics simulation
particle-scale suspension modeling

title: About
text:
Research Engineering
In addition to modeling and experiments, I have hands-on experience designing and fabricating custom research hardware using SolidWorks, resin 3D printing, CNC machining, and graphite milling.
As the first PhD student in a newly formed research group, I have also helped establish laboratory capabilities through procurement, safety, commissioning, maintenance, vendor coordination, and student mentoring.

Jeyaseelan Krishna Udiyappan


PhD Researcher in Chemical Engineering


Electrochemical Systems · Transport Phenomena · Complex Fluids · Multiphysics Modeling


I develop experiments and physics-based models to understand transport in complex electrochemical systems. My work combines electrochemistry, suspension rheology, continuum mechanics, numerical modeling, and custom reactor development, with growing interests in particle-scale suspension dynamics and multiscale computation.
